principles.text: Email your past client list. It is the most overlooked revenue lever; people are just scared to hit send.
Write like a real person. Personality sells; no one wants to reply to a robot or a 'Dear sir/madam' message.
Niche into one specialism and drop service lines where you can't be the best.
Raise your rate as demand for your time grows, and turn away clients who haggle on price.
Traffic that doesn't convert to revenue is worthless. Track each source's cost per conversion and scale the cheaper one.

sampleQA.question: How should I price my freelance or agency work?

answer.text: Increase your hourly rate when demand for your time jumps, and don't accept work below your average rate; low-ball buyers show how they'll behave.
For fixed-scope projects, quote about 20% over your hourly estimate to cover slow payers and scope leeway.
Propose weekly retainers with hourly overage billing, and raise rates every year; a 25% raise is 25% more revenue with no extra hours.
Aim to deliver at least double what you are paid, and know your ROI so you can price with confidence.

sampleQA.question: What's the fastest way to make more money from email?

answer.text: Start by emailing your past client list with a sale or news; most companies miss this and it is fully trackable.
Check deliverability first, write for mobile, use a single call to action, and segment at least customers vs non-customers.
Send a test email and get a second pair of eyes before you hit send; broken personalization tags make an email 10x worse.

sampleQA.question: How do I win more clients on Upwork?

answer.text: Treat it as a funnel: more targeted proposals mean more interviews and jobs, and answer invites within 24 hours.
Open with 'Hey [Name]' using the name from their past feedback, not 'Dear sir/madam'.
Use past-result case studies to land bigger clients, even on a small test slice of their business.
Filter out prospects who want one person doing many jobs for as little as possible.
